qs.q: In MS Excel, a user applies a filter to a dataset. What happens to rows that do not meet the filter criteria?
o: They are transferred automatically to a separate temporary worksheet tab
They are permanently deleted from the underlying worksheet data structure
They are hidden from the current view while remaining intact in the worksheet
They are converted into static text format to prevent accidental editing
They are locked and write-protected from any further user modifications
qs.e: Excel filters hide non-matching rows visually without altering the underlying data or deleting it.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Excel wants to create a chart that shows the proportion of each category in a whole. Which chart type is best?
o: Line chart that shows trends across successive time periods.
Pie chart that depicts each category’s share of the total.
Bar chart that compares values among separate categories.
Scatter plot that illustrates the relationship between two variables.
Histogram that presents the frequency distribution of data values.
qs.e: Pie charts are specifically designed to visualize the relative proportions of categories within a total.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Excel wants to protect a worksheet from accidental edits but allow data entry in specific cells. What is the correct process?
o: Hide the worksheet’s gridlines prior to applying protection.
Lock every cell before enabling worksheet protection.
Unlock the desired cells first, then protect the worksheet.
Assign a password and then protect the worksheet.
Freeze panes before turning on worksheet protection.
qs.e: Cells must be unlocked first; otherwise, protecting the sheet locks all cells by default.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Excel wants to create a dynamic range that expands as new data is added. What feature is used?
o: Create an official Excel table, which expands its range automatically.
Define a named range that uses the OFFSET function for dynamism.
Use a standard filter range that must be adjusted manually.
Build a chart source with a fixed cell‑reference link.
Generate a pivot table that relies on a static data‑source range.
qs.e: Named ranges using OFFSET can dynamically adjust their size based on data changes.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

es.q: Discuss the components and usage of the User Interface in MS Excel according to the course notes.
es.m:
- **Ribbon user interface**: Organises Excel's commands into accessible tabs such as File, Home, Insert, Page Layout, Formulas, Data, Review, and View.
- **Workbooks and worksheets**: A workbook is the Excel file itself, which contains one or more worksheets (tabs) made up of individual cells arranged in rows and columns.
- **Formula Bar**: Located above the grid, it displays the contents of the selected cell and is used for entering or editing formulas.
- **Customizing the user interface**: Users can add frequently used commands to the Quick Access Toolbar and customise the Ribbon to suit their workflow.
es.s: MS Excel — HIT100 Course: Essay questions
